exposure: Prenatal diagnosis (PreND) for congenital heart disease
outcome: Incidence of postnatal shock (serum lactate >4.0 mmol/L or pH <7.2)
cohort: The study included 949 neonates who underwent open heart surgery for congenital heart disease between January 2002 and December 2017.
finding: Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease, despite leading to a higher frequency of postnatal shock, enables earlier intensive care initiation, resulting in a shorter duration and higher resolution rate of shock before surgery.
